title: Definition / population mismatch case: a 30% drop that is mostly a change in who is counted

input.researchQuestion: Did the number of registered vendors on the platform fall between 2021 and 2024?

datasets.description: Fictional 2021 vendor count. Includes inactive vendors.
Fictional 2024 published count. The 2024 methodology note says inactive vendors were dropped from the population.
Fictional 2024 reference table that adds the inactive segment back using the 2021 inactive count (carry-forward).

expectations.text: Because the 2024 methodology note drops inactive vendors, the published 2024 total should fall mechanically even if active vendors are flat.

hypotheses.text: Most of the apparent drop is the change in population definition.

evidence.summary: The 2024 methodology note documents the exclusion of inactive vendors; the naive delta is not a like-for-like change.
On the harmonized population the change shrinks from -30.0% to -8.0%.
A residual -8.0% remains after harmonization, so definition change alone does not explain everything.

requiredLimitations: The 2021 and published 2024 populations differ; the -30.0% figure must not be presented as a decline.
The harmonized 2024 value carries the 2021 inactive segment forward and is a reference value, not an observation.
The residual -8.0% is a change within the active population only.

requiredResearchGaps.need: An observed 2024 count of inactive vendors, or the rule used to flag inactivity in both years.
2022 and 2023 counts under a single definition.

humanReview.notes: A passing report must label the naive comparison NOT_COMPARABLE and must not call the harmonized pair COMPARABLE.
